issues.problem: 40 §7.2 splits each host statically between TS and native (T + TS slots ≤ cores_for_backtest), so native threads stay capped even when the TS queue is empty. Dynamic sharing is only a 'v2 SHOULD', which works against the speed mandate while TS protocol runs and native runs share the fleet.
issues.fix: Make a host-level token pool (TS children and native threads both draw from cores_for_backtest) a v1 SHOULD, with measurement in M6, or at least let the inventory switch a host to native-only while native jobs are queued.

issues.problem: Market-data delay (md) is not applied consistently, so realistic backtests on telonex-delta show the strategy external feeds that are about md (40-140 ms) older relative to the book than live sees. (1) 12 §4.1/K4: on telonex-delta, now = ts_exchange_ms and md enters only through order latencies (13 §6.8). (2) 14 F-7/F-8: the feed clock is max(Telonex local, E). Telonex local time is Telonex's own recorder clock, not the bot's: I re-measured it on btc-updown-15m-1789570800 at p50 +8 ms, p90 +14 ms, p99 +48 ms after the exchange stamp. The TS code assumes this clock includes the 50-150 ms delivery leg (src/backtest/feeds/wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:46-56), and the 110/320 ms latencies were calibrated against the bot's receive clock on the recorded base (parity-harness.md). Result: every realistic decision on Telonex sees Binance and Chainlink values about md older relative to the book than live does. That is exactly the edge that lagsnipe-style strategies trade on. The window gate, TimeWindowGate/DwellGate and rule lookups also run md too early. (3) 13 §8 hard-codes md = 0 for paper, which contradicts §6.8's own derivation that receive-clocked inputs need L_place = md + place. Paper then fills optimistically against V4 backtests, which corrupts the P11/§13.5 baseline. (4) md is one per-run constant that defaults to 0 'until M10', so every realistic run from M3 to M9 uses md = 0. (5) The time at which the strategy-visible overlay (RF10 own orders, depletion) appears is not specified relative to md. 14 Open question 2 leaves all of this open.
issues.fix: Decide before G1 and write it into 12 §4 and 13 §6.8. In realistic, every input is receive-clocked. Telonex rows get a synthesized receipt time R = max(R_prev, E + md_draw), with md_draw from a seeded empirical distribution keyed by (seed, slug, row index). The engine then runs exactly as on V4: now = R, feed clock = R (replacing max(local, E)), the window gate, plugins and the exchange-time estimate use R, and L_place = md + place, L_ack/L_fill = report − md for every input mode. Delete 'md = 0' in 13 §8. Paper uses the live host's md, like V4 uses worker-2's. Specify that own orders and depletion become strategy-visible at exchange-truth time + md, which matches when live sees its own order in the WS book. Measure the md distribution now, at M3, from existing worker-2 V4 packages (receivedAtMs − exchange ts, corrected by the lower-envelope skew estimator of 50 §5.3), not only at M10. Keep the TS feedClockMs only in ts-compat.

issues.problem: Gate 3 makes realistic the default, but the calibration verdict (§12, §11.1 Mode A2) is computed only on decontaminated V4 recordings, while nearly all fleet backtests run on telonex-delta. Telonex has a different cadence, no trade prints (so the queue model falls back to no-prints mode, which is systematically pessimistic for makers: a partly consumed level never fills us) and inferred ticks (11 TT3). §11.4 reports the Telonex readout as information only, and the realistic-on-Telonex vs realistic-on-V4 comparison over overlapping markets is pushed to follow-up F2 (01 §10). So the profile gets approved for an input mode that no threshold checked.
issues.fix: Make the G3 decision per input mode. Add pre-registered metrics for realistic on telonex-delta against live on the calibration markets (C4/C5/C8 equivalents), and pull 'realistic-on-telonex vs realistic-on-V4 on every overlapping worker-2 market, exerciser and lagsnipe' from F2 into M7 as a required report: decision agreement, fill count, maker/taker split and per-market PnL delta with CI. If the Telonex bias is outside thresholds, realistic becomes default only for V4/journal, or Telonex runs carry a flagged, quantified bias.

issues.problem: Nothing measures end-to-end strategy-level agreement between live and backtest, which is the outcome the user cares about. Mode A (§11.1) injects the journaled intents with no strategy running. Mode B only proves determinism. 50 §13.5 compares paper with V4 and is decisions-only and not gated. No metric answers 'if I backtest strategy S on market M, do I get what live got?', including the feedback where fills change later decisions (flatten legs, pending flags, capital).
issues.fix: Add a Mode C (free-running). The probe strategy runs unpinned on the decontaminated V4 recording of each live market, using the fitted realistic ModelConfig on the evaluation half. Compare with the live journal per market: decision agreement (same intent kind, side, price within 1 tick and time within a pre-registered window), fill agreement and PnL error. Pre-register a threshold and make it the headline row of the G3 report. Also report the same paper-vs-V4 free-running comparison for lagsnipe.v15.rs (paper fills simulated) from P11.

issues.problem: §9 models feed visibility as a constant offset (L_b = 110 ms, L_c = 320 ms) in every profile. The measured live Binance latency on the trading machine has a heavy tail: p50 110 ms, p90 171 ms, p99 397 ms (wireBacktestExternalFeeds.ts:28-35). For lag-sniping strategies, the moments when the feed is late are exactly when the edge exists or turns into adverse selection. A constant offset removes that variance, so realistic overstates how fresh feeds are in bursts and cannot be calibrated on the tail. C7 in 51 only checks order-path components.
issues.fix: In realistic only, allow binance.latency and chainlink.latency as distributions (13 §6.8 kinds), drawn per element with RNG keyed by (seed, slug, feed, agg_trade_id or round). Clamp visibility monotonically, vis_i = max(vis_{i−1}, T_i + L_i), so delivery stays in order exactly as the WS delivers. ts-compat keeps the constants. Fit the distributions from V4 receipts (Binance receivedAtMs − T, PolyBolt receipts vs server time) and from live journals. Add the feed legs to the C7 component table with their own thresholds.

issues.problem: §7.2.1 splits each host's CPU statically between TS children and native threads ('T + TS slots MUST NOT exceed cores_for_backtest'), and dynamic sharing is only a SHOULD for v2 (§7.2.3). With today's slots (§2: worker-1 has 6 TS slots of cores_for_backtest 8), native gets T ≤ 2 on worker-1, which conflicts with the default 'T = host TS slot count'. Because TS artifacts still carry most of the load until F1, a static split leaves native threads idle while TS is saturated, or the other way round. That directly cuts fleet throughput.
issues.fix: Put one host-level CPU token pool in v1. The supervisor process already hosts both the TS child pool and the native shim (40 §5.1.1), so one in-process semaphore of cores_for_backtest tokens can gate both TS child job fetches (weight 1) and native admissions (weight per thread). Drop the static inequality. Report token utilization per host in the heartbeat and measure throughput under mixed TS and native load in M6.

issues.problem: Speed is the top priority, but the fleet speedup delivered by this goal applies only to native artifacts: the lagsnipe port and the exerciser. About 80% of fleet markets come from GR protocol runs of TS strategies (41 §1, 16 §9.1), and candidate groups (the largest sweep lever) also need native strategies. Moving protocols to Rust is follow-up F1 (§10, D16). None of §1.1 'Done means', §2 or the M6 proof says that real fleet throughput stays unchanged until F1, so the user may expect a fleet-wide speedup the goal cannot deliver.
issues.fix: State in §1.1 and §2 that fleet throughput gains in this goal are measured on native artifacts only. Schedule the minimum F1 pieces (the build step outside the sandbox from 31, publish authorization, a Rust ENGINE-CONTRACT) right after M6 rather than after M10. Alternatively, allow an early, narrow path such as Rust ports of the top N protocol strategies by volume, so the M6 fleet benchmark reflects real workloads.
issues.userQuestion: The Rust engine only speeds up strategies written in Rust. Your current fleet load (AI protocol sweeps) is TypeScript and stays at today's speed until the follow-up goal. Should the protocol-to-Rust step move earlier (right after fleet integration, before live), or is it fine that the real fleet speedup arrives later?

issues.problem: Decode is the largest measured cost of a single market: about 75 ms against an estimated about 30 ms for C (§3). GZIP is about 44% and decimal strings about 40% of v1 decode (§2.2, DC-9). Yet the structural fix, format v2 or a compact tape cache, is treated as a last resort: DC-9 sets a >40% threshold after DC-1 to DC-5, 15 §4.4 and Open question 1 require user approval because of '52 GB re-conversion', and M-11 waits a week of fleet logs. The repeat pattern is already known: GR screens and coordinate passes re-run the same --latest --limit 1000 set (41 §1). A per-executor RAM LRU cannot hold 1,000 tapes of 7-25 MB, and BullMQ spreads them over 4 hosts. A Rust v1→v2 converter at decode speed would re-convert 31k files in minutes, and with ZSTD plus INT64 the files are likely smaller than v1.
issues.fix: Make 'native v2 tape format' a first-class M5 option: a Rust converter from v1 to v2 (INT64 fixed point, ZSTD, about 64k-row groups, footer keys and sha256), produced as a derived artifact keyed by the v1 file identity. That needs no main or TS converter change before G2. Prove it with an event-stream equality test against the v1 reader. Build a prototype in M1 step 6 to measure decode ms on smoke-50 and heavy-1, and decide at G2 with numbers. Size the disk need from the measured compression ratio.
issues.userQuestion: Rewriting the market files into a faster native format could cut backtest time per market by up to about half. It needs extra disk on each worker (likely 20-30 GB for BTC 15m, possibly replacing the current files later). May the engine build and keep such a derived copy on the workers?

issues.problem: §4.2 compiles dependencies with codegen-units 1 but the strategy crate with codegen-units 16 and no LTO (D18), and §4.1 requires one identical profile for check, iterate and publish. 30 §4 rule 1 and §16 S9 require the engine runtime to be generic over the strategy type. Generic code is codegen'd in the crate that instantiates it, so the whole hot loop (session, OM, ledger, simulator, plugins monomorphized over T) is compiled under the strategy crate's cgu-16, non-LTO settings. The 'deps cgu 1' setting therefore does not help the per-candidate cost C, which 16 §3 names as the main sweep lever after M5. The 16 §11.2 decision rule also ties runtime speed to a warm rebuild of ≤60 s, which only matters for iteration.
issues.fix: Separate the iterate profile from the publish profile. check and iterate keep D18 for fast feedback. publish (and the live build) uses an `artifact-publish` profile: cgu 1 everywhere, thin or fat LTO, optionally PGO with a committed profile file. userQuestions.question: URGENT. Each market's exchange rules (tick size, minimum order size, whether instant orders are held) can only be captured before the market starts. After that they are lost for good. May we start capturing them now, before gate 2? There are two ways: (a) merge only the small capture script to main early, so it runs 24/7 on worker-1, or (b) run it from the branch on this MacBook, which leaves gaps whenever the laptop sleeps. Either way it reads only public Polymarket pages and writes only local files.
userQuestions.recommended: (a). Merge the capture script by itself to main now and run it on worker-1, an always-on Mac mini. It writes local files that are imported into the database later (M3a). This is a one-time exception to 'main untouched until gate 2', and it changes no engine code.
userQuestions.why: Every day without capture means realistic backtests of that day fall back to estimated rules. It is time-sensitive, so it is needed as soon as possible. Source: 40 Open question 5.

userQuestions.question: For speed: may new Rust strategies (not the ported old ones) declare 'only wake me when the best price, my own orders, a price feed or a plugin value changes'? Only about 1 to 16 in 100 market updates change the best prices, so most strategy calls could be skipped. It behaves the same live and in backtests. A strategy may use it only if an automatic check proves its results are exactly the same as without it.
userQuestions.recommended: Yes, as an opt-in option in the first SDK release (the SDK is the library strategies are written against).
userQuestions.why: It is the largest known speedup for parameter sweeps. It is cheap to add now and expensive later, because it shapes the strategy SDK built in M1. Needed at gate 1. Source: 16 Open question 1.

userQuestions.question: Binaries can be built in a way that takes longer to compile but runs faster (link-time optimization, with the strategy compiled directly into the engine). May every binary that the fleet or the live bot runs use the fastest-running build that measurement finds, even if publishing a strategy then takes longer? The estimate is about 7 s warm instead of about 1 s, and more for the heaviest settings. Is there a rebuild-time limit?
userQuestions.recommended: Yes. Published, fleet and live binaries use the fastest-running build, as long as results stay identical and builds stay reproducible. The quick build stays for local checks. No hard limit in this goal: build times are reported, and a limit (for example 60 s warm on an M4 mini) is set when AI protocols start writing Rust strategies.
userQuestions.why: Speed is the top priority, but build time will matter once agents iterate on Rust strategies. This amends D18. Needed at gate 1. Sources: 01 Open question 2, 31 Open question 3, 12 Open question 2.

userQuestions.question: On Polymarket today, an instant (FOK/FAK) BUY is sized in dollars, not shares. When a strategy asks to buy '10 shares' instantly, should realistic mode and the live bot (a) turn it into a dollar amount at the limit price (10 x limit)? That can give slightly more than 10 shares when the price is better than the limit, exactly as the exchange would. Or (b) reject the order, so every strategy must state how many dollars to spend?
userQuestions.recommended: (a). It matches the exchange, ported strategies like lagsnipe keep working, and a per-market report shows shares received vs requested. Copy mode keeps share sizing.
userQuestions.why: It changes position sizes of ported strategies in realistic mode and live. Needed at gate 1. Source: 10 Open question 1.

userQuestions.question: Worker-2's recordings contain feeds that the Telonex history does not have: Binance best bid/ask (bookTicker), Chainlink TWAP (a time-averaged price) and an opening-TWAP price to beat. Should Rust strategies be able to use them on recordings, in paper mode and live in this goal, or should they stay rejected until a follow-up?
userQuestions.recommended: Follow-up. A strategy that uses them could not be backtested on the Telonex history that most fleet runs use. Revisit after calibration, starting with the opening-TWAP price to beat, which may match how Polymarket settles markets.
userQuestions.why: This is a scope decision, and scope changes need you (R11). Needed at gate 1. Source: 14 Open question 3.

userQuestions.question: Real orders must be possible only in a special build (D05), but the live bot should run exactly the binary that was backtested (D17), and a special build is by definition a different file. Choose: (a) one binary for everything that contains the order-sending code, with real orders blocked only at launch (flag, config, launcher checks, key lock); or (b) two builds from the same source. In (b), the normal build serves fleet, backtest and paper. The real-order build is made by you on the live Mac and never sent to the fleet. It is linked to the normal one by a source fingerprint and by identical decisions on replayed markets.
userQuestions.recommended: (b). Fleet and agent binaries then physically cannot place orders. If the M6 comparison shows Macs producing different bytes from the same source, also pin one Xcode Command Line Tools version on every Mac.
userQuestions.why: A safety rule (R10) depends on it. Needed at gate 1. Sources: 20 Open question 1, 31 Open questions 1 and 4.

userQuestions.question: Some tests must be written by a separate AI that never sees the engine code, so it cannot repeat the builder's mistakes. It also double-checks every difference that changes money. Who writes these tests: Fable, or a separate Claude session? And who starts it: you, or the launcher that starts the main session?
userQuestions.recommended: Fable, started automatically by the launcher right after gate 1, in its own checkout with the engine sources blocked. A different model is less likely to share the builder's blind spots.
userQuestions.why: Gate 2 cannot pass without these tests, so the answer is needed at gate 1. Source: 60 Open question 2.

userQuestions.question: A faster local copy of the market files makes reading a market about 10 times faster (about 5 ms instead of 45-70 ms) and could roughly halve the time per market. The original files stay untouched. The copy needs about 23-26 GB per backtest Mac today and grows with new data. (a) May the engine keep this copy for the benchmark sets on this MacBook before gate 2? That is about 1 GB, but only 2.5 GB is free, so you would need to free space. (b) May it keep the copy on all fleet Macs after gate 2, and is there a disk limit per Mac? Related: should we ever re-convert all ~31,000 original files (52 GB plus the R2 copies) into a new format? And may native workers keep a size-limited cache of files downloaded from R2, instead of downloading them again on every run?
userQuestions.recommended: (a) Yes; free about 10 GB on this MacBook. (b) Yes in principle, with a cap you set per Mac (for example 40 GB), and the final yes at gate 2 with measured numbers. Do not re-convert the original files: the local copy gives the speed without touching the main dataset or R2. Allow a size-limited download cache on workers (for example 20 GB, oldest files removed first).
userQuestions.why: Reading the files is the largest single cost per market. Part (a) is needed before the first benchmark (M1 step 7), part (b) at gate 2. Sources: 16 Open question 2, 01 Open question 3, 15 Open questions 1 and 3.

userQuestions.question: Speed benchmarks need this MacBook idle for several hours (no other backtests or AI sessions, on power, lid open). A nightly automatic copy-mode check would also run here. May the agent run these unattended, and when must it not run them (for example while you work, or while a live or paper bot runs)?
userQuestions.recommended: Yes, overnight (for example 01:00-07:00) while the Mac is on power, and never while a live or paper session you started is running. After gate 4, move the nightly checks to a worker Mac.
userQuestions.why: Until you answer, benchmark numbers are marked 'non-idle' and cannot be used to compare milestones. Needed before M1 step 7. Sources: 16 Open question 3, 60 Open question 3.

userQuestions.question: Three storage permissions are needed: (1) uploading native binaries; (2) a private bucket for live journals and live order records, written only by the live Mac; (3) uploading per-order records ('ledgers') of backtests from the aggregate host, worker-1. Should each have its own R2 bucket or token, held only by the machine that needs it?

userQuestions.question: Polymarket changed its fee formula several times, so a realistic backtest from Dec 2025 to Oct 2026 crosses four fee periods, and D21 says results should not be pooled across them. Should such a run be (a) refused, (b) split automatically into one run per fee period, or (c) allowed, with extra per-period statistics and a 'mixed fee periods' badge on the dashboard?
userQuestions.recommended: (c) as the default.
userQuestions.why: Typical backtests (--latest --limit 1000) cross fee periods, so refusing them would block normal use. Needed before realistic mode (M3b). Source: 42 Open question 1.

userQuestions.question: There are two gaps in the history before mid-2026. (1) How long Polymarket held instant orders before 2026-08-17 is known only from news and blog posts, not from Polymarket's own changelog. Should markets from before that date count as evidence for making realistic mode the default, or only markets from 2026-08-17 on? (2) The fees actually charged in January-May 2026 must be checked. Is the free Polymarket Data API path acceptable, with Telonex's paid on-chain fills data bought only if the free API cannot reach back to January?
userQuestions.recommended: (1) Use the reported values but flag those markets, and count only markets from 2026-08-17 on as gate-3 evidence. (2) Yes, free path first; buy Telonex data only if needed, after you see the price. Periods that stay unverified are marked 'fee unverified' and do not count toward gate 3.
userQuestions.why: Most of the Telonex history is from Dec 2025-Aug 2026, so this decides how far realistic mode can be trusted on it. Needed by M3b. Sources: 11 Open questions 1 and 2.

userQuestions.question: Polymarket does not document what happens when our instant order meets our own resting order. Should the ~$5 rules budget include one deliberate $1 test where we trade against ourselves? Or should our engine never send an order that would trade against our own resting order (in backtest and live alike), so the exchange's behavior never matters?
userQuestions.recommended: No test. Block orders that would cross our own resting orders, the same way in backtest and live. It costs nothing and avoids a deliberate trade with ourselves, which can look like wash trading. Copy mode is unaffected.
userQuestions.why: The current simulator rule is a guess, and either answer removes it. Needed by M3b. Source: 13 Open question 1.

(b) Keep worker-2 at about 3 slots' worth, so its recordings stay clean. (c) Yes until gate 4, then no while live or calibration runs. (d) Yes: calibration first, then your runs, then agents.

userQuestions.question: M8 needs paper trading: live public market data, simulated fills, no keys and no order-sending code. May the agent run it on this MacBook? Strategies that use the Chainlink price, such as lagsnipe, need a Polymarket API key for that feed, and the agent may never hold your keys. Choose: (a) the agent runs only strategies without Chainlink, and you launch the Chainlink paper sessions; (b) you create an API key on a separate wallet with no funds, which the agent may use only for paper market data; (c) get Chainlink from another source (this changes the feed model; not recommended).
userQuestions.recommended: Yes to agent-run paper mode, and (b): a key of an empty wallet can neither spend money nor cancel your real orders, and it lets the lagsnipe paper rehearsals run without you. Until then, (a) applies.
userQuestions.why: Option (b) is a narrow, explicit exception to safety rule R10 that only you can grant. Needed by M8. Sources: 01 Open question 10, 50 Open question 7.

userQuestions.question: Network distance to Polymarket is by far the largest part of order delay: about 70-380 ms per order, against under 0.3 ms inside our code. Calibration results apply only to the machine and network that produced them. Where should calibration and live trading run? Options: this MacBook (today's live Mac); worker-2 next to the recorder (easier comparison, but not the live machine); or later a Linux server closer to Polymarket in a permitted region, where calibration would be repeated. Can you also provide one small cloud server for a network measurement in M9?
userQuestions.recommended: Calibrate on the Mac that will trade live afterwards: this MacBook, kept at home on power, with backtests and AI sessions paused during the runs. Yes to one small cloud server in a permitted region, for the M9 network measurement only. Decide whether to move live trading after seeing those numbers.
userQuestions.why: Needed by M9, before gate 4. Sources: 50 Open question 3, 51 Open question 3.

userQuestions.question: Which wallet sends real orders: a plain wallet (EOA, signature type 0) or your existing SAFE/relayer setup (type 2)?
userQuestions.recommended: A new, dedicated plain wallet (EOA) funded with about $100 for calibration. It is the simplest signing path, nothing else is at risk, and it is separate from your other bots: a missed heartbeat (the exchange's keep-alive signal) cancels every order of one key. Add SAFE support later if live trading needs it.
userQuestions.why: It decides the signing and approval code of the order adapter. Needed by M9. Source: 50 Open question 1.

userQuestions.question: Which phone push service should send live alerts (kill switch, loss stop, connection gaps, strategy crash, bursts of rejected orders): a Telegram bot or ntfy? And which account receives them?
userQuestions.recommended: ntfy with a private, random topic name: no account needed, one simple web request per alert, and apps for iOS and Android.
userQuestions.why: Needed by M9. Source: 50 Open question 2.

userQuestions.question: If the live bot crashes in real-money mode, may it restart itself? The proposal is up to 3 restarts per hour, each time cancelling open orders, re-reading positions and sending an alert. Or should it stay stopped until you restart it?
userQuestions.recommended: Allow up to 3 automatic restarts per hour with an alert each time, then stay stopped. The $60 total loss stop carries over across restarts.
userQuestions.why: Needed by M9. Source: 50 Open question 4.

userQuestions.question: The calibration pass marks (D35) were frozen with eight checks. Three additions are proposed. (1) Price-feed delays (Binance, Chainlink) must also match in the slowest 1% (99th percentile within +/-30%), because the edge of lag-sniping strategies is decided there. (2) Settlement delays, which are seconds rather than milliseconds, are judged only on the +/-20% rule, not the 10 ms rule. (3) Two end-to-end checks: a free-running backtest of the probe strategy makes at least 90% of the same decisions as live, and the average profit error is at most 1 cent per share. Plus a separate verdict for Telonex data, which most fleet backtests use. Do you accept these?
userQuestions.recommended: Accept all three, with 90% and 1 cent, frozen before the first real order.
userQuestions.why: Pass marks must be fixed before the run so nobody can move the goalposts. Needed by gate 4. Sources: 14 Open question 6, 51 Open questions 2 and 5.

userQuestions.question: With $30 for resting-order (maker) tests, the maker fill-rate check may end borderline or with 'not enough data'. May the maker phase then go beyond $30, which would also raise the $60 total stop? Or do we accept a borderline result with that limitation flagged?
userQuestions.recommended: Accept a borderline result with the limitation flagged. Decide on any extension after reading the calibration report, as a separate run.
userQuestions.why: This is a money decision, and only you can raise the budget. Needed by gate 4 at the latest. Source: 51 Open question 1.
